summary: Regional latency spike — cross-region routing causing slow responses for customer requests
description: Issue summary: Customer reported a sudden increase in inference latency and intermittent request timeouts starting 2026-02-25 09:10 UTC. Impact: customer-facing inference calls experienced 5-15s p95 latency and several 504s, affecting production traffic for a dedicated account. Environment: Redwood hosted prod region us-east; Dedicated capacity for FinTree located in us-east but traffic observed routing to eu-west.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues inference calls to Redwood API endpoint with region hint 'us-east'
2) Observe request traces showing upstream host in eu-west
3) P95 latency increases to 5-15s and occasional 504s are returned
4) Reverting routing to strict region affinity returns latency to baseline (~200-500ms p95)
logs: 2026-02-25T09:12:03Z api-gateway WARN request_id=abc123 routed_to=eu-west latency=12034ms status=200
2026-02-25T09:15:38Z network INFO control-plane: route-policy applied=geo-fallback-v2 changed=true by=deploy-service
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: serving runtime regression or busy GPUs causing increased token latency.
Correlation: multiple distinct customers in us-east reported elevated latency between 09:10-09:40 UTC.
Tracing: distributed traces show client requests entering us-east edge but being forwarded to eu-west inference hosts (50-70% of requests during window).
Control plane change: deploy-service pipeline pushed 'geo-fallback-v2' at 09:05 UTC which relaxed strict region affinity for routing during capacity shortages.
Network check: no reported BGP/ISP outage for us-east; edge health checks for us-east gateway showed transient error spike starting 09:08 UTC causing routing policy to prefer eu-west.
Reproduction: manually forcing region-affinity at edge eliminated cross-region routing and returned p95 latency to expected levels (~300ms).
Temporary mitigation: rolled back 'geo-fallback-v2' and reinstated 'geo-affinity-v1' at 09:42 UTC.
comments: 2026-02-25 09:20 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer reports "inference calls are taking 10+ seconds and some calls time out". Collected request IDs and asked for sample traces.
2026-02-25 09:28 - SRE (Daniel Park): Noted change to routing policy 'geo-fallback-v2' deployed at 09:05. Kicked off initial trace analysis; forwarding to Networking and Routing teams.

2026-02-25 09:38 - Networking (Maya Thompson): Edge health checks for us-east showing increased 502/504 between 09:07-09:20; reason: spike in control-plane error causing unhealthy-marking and failover.

2026-02-25 09:42 - SRE (Daniel Park): Rolled back routing policy to 'geo-affinity-v1' (manual rollback). Observed drop in cross-region routing from ~60% to ~2% and p95 latency returned to baseline within 3 minutes.
2026-02-25 10:05 - Support (Aisha Khan): Notified customer of mitigation and temporary workaround. Customer confirmed reduced latency and no ongoing timeouts.
2026-02-27 11:15 - Eng (Omar Ruiz): Deployed follow-up fix to rate-limiter in edge health check probe to reduce false unhealthy signals; added canary checks to routing rollout pipeline.
2026-02-28 15:30 - Support (Aisha Khan): Closed loop with customer; provided incident summary and next steps for durable fixes.
root_cause: A recent routing policy change ('geo-fallback-v2') relaxed strict regional affinity. Combined with transient control-plane health-check instability in the us-east edge, a large fraction of production requests were routed to eu-west hosts, increasing network latency and causing timeouts for region-sensitive customer workloads.
resolution: Rolled back routing policy to 'geo-affinity-v1' to restore strict region affinity; applied fix to edge health-check rate limiter to avoid false unhealthy markings; added canary and staged rollout checks to routing policy pipeline. Customer notified and latencies returned to baseline.
postmortem_actions: 1) Improve routing rollouts: add canary and automated rollback gates to control-plane pipeline
2) Harden edge health checks: tune rate-limit and thresholds to reduce transient unhealthy markings
3) Add alerting: p95 cross-region routing percentage alert and per-customer region-affinity SLO monitor
4) Customer follow-up: provide config guide for region pinning in client SDKs and recommend dedicated routing policy for high-sensitivity customers
